Before you turn it on

%1$s adds virtual bass and a gentle correction to the built-in speaker of your phone. It is an unofficial fork of RootlessJamesDSP; it is not made or supported by the RootlessJamesDSP or JamesDSP developers. It comes with no warranty (GPL-3.0).

Setup, no root needed: two permissions must be granted once from a shell, for the package %2$s.
• Shizuku (recommended, no PC): install Shizuku, start it with wireless debugging, then allow access in the setup screens of this app.
• ADB (with a PC): enable USB debugging and run
%3$s
(the last line is optional: automatic start after reboot).

Android 15 and later: in Developer options turn on "Disable screen share protections", otherwise notifications are hidden while audio is captured.

Apps that block audio capture (for example Spotify, Chrome, SoundCloud) play unprocessed. Processing applies to the built-in speaker only. Virtual bass adds about 0.15 s of delay.

Privacy: only the settings of this app are stored on this phone. No song titles, no recordings, no usage data. Nothing is sent anywhere; the only network access is the optional AutoEQ search, which contacts the AutoEQ server of the original project.

%1$s stores on this phone only:
• its settings (speaker correction, virtual bass, app options),
• the last loudness-match level (one number),
• a technical log in the app cache, rewritten at every start; it leaves the phone only if you share it under Troubleshooting.

It does not store song titles, artists or any audio, and it records nothing from the microphone. System audio is processed in memory while the service runs and is not saved.

Nothing is sent anywhere. The only network access is the optional AutoEQ search in the JamesDSP equalizer, which contacts the AutoEQ server of the original project (aeq.timschneeberger.me) when you use it.

The virtual bass settings are excluded from Android cloud backup and device transfer.

Order: JamesDSP effects → %1$s. Both are applied together; %1$s runs last, so its limiter is the final speaker protection. While %1$s processes, JamesDSP bass boost, analog modelling and output control are locked.
During blind comparisons, measurements and buzz diagnostics only %1$s runs (JamesDSP effects are skipped).
Locked while %1$s virtual bass is on. Your settings are kept and apply again when %1$s is off.
Locked while %1$s virtual bass is on: the JamesDSP output runs at 0 dB with its limiter off, and the %1$s limiter is the last stage. Your settings are kept and apply again when %1$s is off.
Applied before %1$s. The compressor changes the levels the %1$s virtual bass reacts to.
Adds to the %1$s EQ. Large low boosts make the %1$s limiter work harder.
More fullness (recommended)
Adds body, fullness and resonance to instruments. Conservative, so buzzing is unlikely.
Deep bass (experimental)
Tries to reproduce bass below what the speaker can play. Varies a lot between songs and can buzz.
